_doc: Source ledger for chokepoint / headline shares. Each entry ties a figure to a NAMED source AND the quoted table row / sentence, so a bare citation cannot hide a misread. Rule: a chokepoint tagged conf=measured MUST have an entry here whose quoted row supports its share; if the source has no computable figure, the tag is estimate/attributed. check.py enforces presence (check_ledger).
_method: USGS MCS PDFs fetched with a browser User-Agent (default fetch UA gets 403); extracted with `pdftotext -raw`. USE THE LATEST EDITION (MCS 2026): USGS revises prior-year numbers substantially between editions (e.g. rhenium world 62->81 t; strontium Iran 39->56%; tungsten world 81->85 kt). Shares below are from the MCS 2026 (2025-data) column.

phosphate-food.quoted_row: Morocco 33,000 30,000 50,000,000 | World total (rounded) 233,000 240,000 74,000,000 (cols: 2023 prod, 2024 prod, reserves)

pgm-catalyst.claim: South Africa ~78% of world PGM reserves (platinum ~71%; palladium Russia-led)
pgm-catalyst.quoted_row: South Africa ... 125,000 120,000 63,000,000 | World total ... 179,000 170,000 >81,000,000; 'resources and reserves are in the Bushveld Complex in South Africa'

steel-alloys.source: USGS MCS 2026 — Niobium; USGS MCS 2026 — Vanadium
steel-alloys.quoted_row: Niobium: 'Brazil ~92% of global production'. Vanadium: China e84,000 82,000 5,800 | World total 118,000 110,000 21,000
steel-alloys.computed: niobium 92%; vanadium 82,000/110,000 = 75% (2025) — MCS2025 gave 70%, revised up.

boron.claim: Turkey ~73% of world borate reserves (Eti Maden company estimate)
boron.source: USGS MCS 2025 — Boron (no world total); Eti Maden (company claim)
boron.quoted_row: 'World total4 XX XX XX' + footnote 4: 'World totals cannot be calculated because production and reserves are not reported in a consistent manner by all countries.' The '~70%' had been misread from 'About 70% of all deposits in Turkey are colemanite' (deposit TYPE, not world share).
boron.computed: NO world reserves total exists in USGS -> a world % is not computable; ~73% is Eti Maden's own claim, hence estimate

tungsten.claim: China ~79% of world tungsten mine production
tungsten.computed: 67,000/85,000 = 78.8% -> ~79% (2025). NOTE: MCS2025 gave 67,000/81,000=83%; USGS revised world up to 85,000 -> back to ~79% (original atlas ~80% was right).

strontium.computed: Iran 250,000/450,000 = 56% (2025); Spain 100,000 = 22%; China 80,000 = 18%. NOTE: MCS2025 gave Iran 39% (tied Spain); USGS revised -> Iran is the clear leader ~56%. Original atlas ~58% was ~right.

gallium.claim: China ~98% of world primary (low-purity) gallium production
gallium.quoted_row: 'China accounted for 99% of worldwide primary low-purity gallium production.'
gallium.computed: USGS says 99%; atlas ~98% is within rounding

bismuth.quoted_row: China 13,300 13,000 NA | World total (rounded) 16,200 16,000 NA; 'China, the leading producer and exporter'

germanium.quoted_row: 'China continued to be the leading global producer and exporter of germanium metal'; 'most producers do not publicly report germanium' output.
germanium.computed: USGS publishes NO country production table for germanium -> ~60% is an industry estimate, not measurable; retagged estimate

antimony.claim: China refining chokepoint (mine ~60%; refining/oxide dominance is the binding stage)
antimony.quoted_row: China e62,300 60,000 670,000 | World total (rounded) 106,000 100,000 >2,000,000; US import 'Oxide: China 76%'
antimony.computed: mine 60,000/100,000 = 60%; chokepoint is refining/oxide + Sep-2024 export controls, not the mine share

beryllium.claim: United States ~53% of world beryllium production
beryllium.quoted_row: United States 230 230 | China e78 77 | Brazil e80 80 | World total (rounded) 433 430
beryllium.computed: US 230/430 = 53% (2025). MCS2025 gave 180/360=50%; USGS revised US up to 230.

fluorine.claim: China ~60% of world fluorspar mine production

displays-indium.quoted_row: 'China is the leading global producer of Indium, accounting for 70% of the world total.'

nickel.claim: Indonesia ~61% of world nickel mine production

cobalt.source: USGS MCS 2025 — Cobalt (mine); refining share is industry/IEA
cobalt.quoted_row: Congo (Kinshasa) 175,000 220,000 6,000,000 | World total (rounded) 238,000 290,000 11,000,000; 'China was the world's leading producer of refined cobalt'
cobalt.computed: DRC mine 220,000/290,000 = 76% (USGS-measured). China refine ~75% is USGS-qualitative + industry — PENDING an IEA/Cobalt-Institute source for the exact %

molybdenum.claim: China ~40% of world molybdenum mine production (diversified — not a chokepoint)

rhenium.claim: aerospace: world ~81 t rhenium; Chile ~37% (largest single source)
rhenium.quoted_row: Chile9 29,000 30,000 1,300,000 | World total (rounded) 79,800 81,000 Large; 'Estimated world rhenium production in 2025 increased 1% to 81,000 kg'
rhenium.computed: Chile 30,000/81,000 = 37% (2025). '~81 t world' is correct; the atlas's 'Chile 55%' was WRONG -> corrected to ~37%. (Note: MCS2025 listed world 62,000; USGS revised up in the 2026 edition.)

manganese.claim: China ~90% of battery-grade manganese (sulphate/EMM) — processing, not mine
manganese.source: USGS MCS 2025 (mine, diversified); battery-grade share is industry/IEA
manganese.computed: USGS MINE: China 770/20,000 = 4% (South Africa leads). The ~90% is battery-grade processing (industry/IEA), a different stage — PENDING that source

magnesium.computed: row footnote merged in pdftotext; China clearly dominant (~90-95% of ~1,000 kt) — atlas ~87% plausible; PENDING a clean re-extraction
